Container.Name: Hermes-Agent
Container.Overview: The self-improving AI agent built by Nous Research. The only agent with a built-in learning loop.
Container.Changes:
### 2026.07.17 - Fix dashboard startup after the upstream authentication hardening: replace the deprecated HERMES_DASHBOARD_INSECURE setting with required username/password authentication. - Existing installs must add HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME and HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD to the container settings. HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_SECRET is optional but recommended so login sessions survive container restarts.
### 2026.06.03 - Fix WebUI not loading: add HERMES_DASHBOARD_INSECURE=1 so the dashboard binds on 0.0.0.0 (the OAuth gate otherwise refuses to bind and the WebUI never opens). - Fix permission errors: HERMES_UID/HERMES_GID now default to 10000 (the image rejects values below 1000, so the old 99/100 defaults silently fell back to 10000 and broke writes to /opt/data/pairing). Existing installs may need: chown -R 10000:10000 /mnt/cache/appdata/hermes-agent

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: The /opt/data volume is the single source of truth for all Hermes state. Must be owned by HERMES_UID:HERMES_GID (default 10000:10000). If you see permission errors after first run or after an upgrade, run on the host: chown -R 10000:10000 /mnt/cache/appdata/hermes-agent (the 'pairing' subfolder is the one that commonly breaks). Use a real disk path like /mnt/cache/... - on the /mnt/user FUSE share the container's ownership fix can fail to stick.

Config.Name: Dashboard
Config.Description: Port for the dashboard HTTP server

Config.Name: HERMES_DASHBOARD
Config.Description: Set to 1 (or true / yes) to launch the dashboard alongside the main command

Config.Name: HERMES_DASHBOARD_HOST
Config.Description: Bind address for the dashboard HTTP server

Config.Name: HERMES_DASHBOARD_PORT
Config.Description: Port for the dashboard HTTP server

Config.Name: HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD
Config.Description: Required password for the dashboard login. Use a strong password and keep the dashboard on a trusted LAN or VPN; do not expose it directly to the internet.

Config.Name: HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_SECRET
Config.Description: Optional but recommended signing secret so dashboard login sessions survive container restarts. Use at least 32 random bytes, for example the output of: openssl rand -hex 32. If left blank, Hermes generates a new secret at each start and existing sessions are signed out.

Config.Name: TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS
Config.Description: Comma-separated user IDs allowed to use the bot (applies to DMs, groups, and forums)

Config.Name: TELEGRAM_GROUP_ALLOWED_USERS
Config.Description: Comma-separated sender user IDs authorized in groups/forums only (does NOT grant DM access). Chat-ID-shaped values (starting with -) are still honored as chat IDs for backward compat with pre-#17686 configs, with a deprecation warning.

Config.Name: TELEGRAM_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS
Config.Description: Comma-separated group/forum chat IDs; any member is authorized

Config.Name: HERMES_GID
Config.Description: Runtime group ID. Must be 1000-65534 - the image silently rejects lower values, so Unraid's default 100 (users) will NOT work and the container falls back to GID 10000. Leave at 10000 unless you need to match a host group >=1000. The appdata directory must be owned by this GID.

Config.Name: HERMES_UID
Config.Description: Runtime user ID. Must be 1000-65534 - the image silently rejects lower values, so Unraid's default 99 (nobody) will NOT work and the container falls back to UID 10000. Leave at 10000 unless you need to match a host user >=1000. The appdata directory must be owned by this UID. If you hit permission errors (e.g. 'Permission denied: /opt/data/pairing/telegram-approved.json'), fix ownership on the host: chown -R 10000:10000 /mnt/cache/appdata/hermes-agent
